full_judgment:
2. This Criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 6-3-2019 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.26330 of 2019 filed on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure disposing of the said application summarily and allowing respondent No.1 in obtaining opinion of the handwriting expert of CID. 

 The complainant-petitioner filed Complaint Case No.128 of 2013 under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 against respondent No.1 alleging that respondent No.1 took loan of Taka 80,00,000 from the complainant. In order to adjust the loan, he issued two cheques of Taka 80,00,000 dated 18-12-2012 and 26-12-2012 from his own account maintained in Southeast Bank Limited, Dhaka. On 6-1-2013, the complainant deposited both the cheques for encashment but the cheques were returned unpaid for insufficient of fund. On 14-1-2013 and 21-1-2013, the complainant-petitioner through his learned Advocate sent two legal notices at two different addresses of respondent No.1 but he did not pay the money within 30 days. It is alleged that respondent No.1 defalcated to pay the money of the complainant. Soon after completion of required formalities, the case record was transferred to the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka and was registered as Metropolitan Case No.128 of 2013. 

 9. A complaint filed under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is disposed of in a summary way and, as such, the trial of this case cannot be prolonged for indefinite period in the name of obtaining opinion of the handwriting expert. Moreover, the application for obtaining opinion of the handwriting expert was filed at the belated stage of the trial and, as such, the High Court Division was not justified in allowing the application for handwriting expert. In such view of the matter, we are inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment. Accordingly, the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.26330 of 2019 is set-aside and the prayer for obtaining the opinion of the handwriting expert is rejected. 

 The trial Court is directed to dispose of Metropolitan Sessions Case No.7700 of 2013 as expeditiously as possible.
